title: The residue-field fibre module is the localization of the prime quotient
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, and let $N$ be a $B$-module. Put $U=\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)$ and $M=N/\mathfrak pN$, where $\mathfrak pN$ is the $B$-submodule generated by $\varphi(a)n$ for $a\in\mathfrak p$, $n\in N$. There is a canonical $B$-linear isomorphism $N\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong U^{-1}M$ sending $n\otimes\overline{a/s}$ to $\overline{\varphi(a)n}/\varphi(s)$; its inverse sends $\bar n/\varphi(s)$ to $n\otimes\overline{1/s}$. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)= (A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field of the ring prime $\mathfrak p$, tensor is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Moreover, if $\mathfrak q\subset B$ is prime with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ and $z\in M$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak q$, then $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z/1)=\mathfrak q$ in $U^{-1}M$, and hence the image of $z/1$ in the fibre has the same annihilator [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), Lemma Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact) specialized to a prime quotient, and Lemma Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), proof of (2); together these give the module form of the fundamental diagram and the localized annihilator witness.

proof.text: Write S=A\setminus\mathfrak p. It is multiplicatively closed because \mathfrak p is prime, and U=\varphi(S) is multiplicatively closed in B. By the explicit definition \kappa(\mathfrak p)=S^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p), write its elements as \overline a/\overline s with s\in S. The quotient map N\to M=N/\mathfrak pN is B-linear, and the relations defining \mathfrak pN are exactly that every \varphi(r)n with r\in\mathfrak p becomes zero. The quotient-tensor lemma [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] gives the standard identification of (A/\mathfrak p)\otimes_A N with M (up to the symmetry of tensor factors).

source.place: Lemma Tags 00DF and 00DK, with the residue-field construction at a prime.

proof.text: Define on pure tensors \Psi(n\otimes(\overline a/\overline s))=\overline{\varphi(a)n}/\varphi(s). This is balanced in n and in the fraction: changing n by an element of \mathfrak pN changes the numerator by zero, and the equality criterion for fractions in S^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p) says that two representatives become equal after multiplication by an element of S; the same multiplier lies in U and therefore gives the equality criterion in U^{-1}M. The tensor balancing relation gives \Psi(an\otimes r)=\Psi(n\otimes\overline a r), so the formula descends to an A-linear map N\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to U^{-1}M. It is B-linear because B acts on the numerator through its action on N and on M.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), fraction construction and balancing check.

proof.text: Define \Theta:U^{-1}M\to N\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p) by \Theta(\bar n/\varphi(s))=n\otimes\overline{1/s}. If n is changed by \mathfrak pN, each added term has the form \varphi(r)n' with r\in\mathfrak p and maps to n'\otimes\overline{r/s}=0. If a localization equality is witnessed by u=\varphi(t)\in U, then multiplication by \overline t is invertible in \kappa(\mathfrak p), so the corresponding tensors are equal; hence \Theta is well defined. On generators, \Theta\Psi(n\otimes\overline a/\overline s)=n\otimes\overline{a/s}=n\otimes\overline a\,\overline{1/s} and \Psi\Theta(\bar n/\varphi(s))=\bar n/\varphi(s). Thus \Psi and \Theta are inverse B-linear isomorphisms, with exactly the displayed formulas.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00DK, explicit inverse and verification of the tensor-localization isomorphism.

proof.text: Now assume\mathfrak q is prime, \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p, and \operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak q. For b\in B, the localization zero criterion says b(z/1)=0 in U^{-1}M exactly when some u\in U satisfies ubz=0 in M. Writing u=\varphi(s) with s\notin\mathfrak p, this means ub\in\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak q. Since u\notin\mathfrak q (otherwise s\in\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p) and \mathfrak q is prime, b\in\mathfrak q. The reverse inclusion is immediate from bz=0, so \operatorname{Ann}_B(z/1)=\mathfrak q.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), proof of (2), specialized to U=\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p).

proof.text: Finally, the canonical isomorphism \Psi is B-linear, so it preserves annihilators of corresponding elements. The element z/1 therefore corresponds to the fibre element represented by z\otimes\overline1, and that element has annihilator \mathfrak q as well. By the annihilator definition of associated primes [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], this is precisely the asserted associated-prime witness in the fibre.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05BZ, conclusion of the localized annihilator witness.

split_report.summary: Read the item against Stacks Tags 00DK, 00DF and 05BZ. Kept the exact hypotheses and conclusion, and supplied a direct fraction-calculus proof: identify the residue field with the localization of A/p, construct the canonical B-linear maps in both directions, verify their well-definedness and inverse formulas, then prove the annihilator equality using the localization zero criterion, contraction hypothesis and primality. No new nodes were needed; existing quotient-tensor Mathlib leaf is cited. Corrected the coefficient field: for a ring prime, κ(p) is explicitly S⁻¹(A/p); the scheme-point residue-field node was inapplicable.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the supporting commutative-algebra reduction in lem-trf-local-term-locality described by the Tag 05C2/00DK localization step.

lean.statement: theorem fibreModuleLocalization (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] : letI : Algebra A B := φ.toAlgebra letI : Module A N := Module.compHom N φ haveI : IsScalarTower A B N := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl ∃ e : TensorProduct A N p.ResidueField ≃ₗ[B] LocalizedModule (Submonoid.map φ p.primeCompl) (N ⧸ Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n}), (∀ (n : N) (a : A) (s : p.primeCompl), e (TensorProduct.tmul A n (algebraMap A p.ResidueField a * (algebraMap A p.ResidueField s.1)⁻¹)) = LocalizedModule.mk (Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n}) (φ a • n)) (⟨φ s.1, Submonoid.mem_map_of_mem φ s.property⟩ : Submonoid.map φ p.primeCompl)) ∧ (∀ (n : N) (s : p.primeCompl), e.symm (LocalizedModule.mk (Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n}) n) (⟨φ s.1, Submonoid.mem_map_of_mem φ s.property⟩ : Submonoid.map φ p.primeCompl)) = TensorProduct.tmul A n (algebraMap A p.ResidueField 1 * (algebraMap A p.ResidueField s.1)⁻¹)) ∧ (∀ (q : Ideal B), q.IsPrime → q.comap φ = p → ∀ z : N ⧸ Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n}, (⊥ : Submodule B (N ⧸ Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n})).colon {z} = q → (⊥ : Submodule B (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.map φ p.primeCompl) (N ⧸ Submodule.span B {x : N | ∃ (a : A) (n : N), a ∈ p ∧ x = φ a • n}))).colon {LocalizedModule.mk z 1} = q ∧ (⊥ : Submodule B (TensorProduct A N p.ResidueField)).colon {e.symm (LocalizedModule.mk z 1)} = q)
